changes.was:
${equationHTML(est)}

f(n) estimates how many guesses are still needed from a position whose candidate set has effective size n = 2H, where H is the entropy in bits of the candidates under the prior. With a uniform prior that is simply how many candidates are left; as the prior concentrates on a few of them it shrinks toward 1.

${table}

The coefficients are fitted by policy iteration — play many games with the current f, record what each position actually cost, refit, repeat — over the ${est.form} family (${est.description}). The result is floored at 1, since one more guess is always needed.
changes.now:
${equationHTML(est)}

f(n) estimates how many guesses are still needed from a position whose candidate set has effective size n = 2H, where H is the entropy in bits of the candidates under the prior. With a uniform prior that is simply how many candidates are left; as the prior concentrates on a few of them it shrinks toward 1.

${table}

The coefficients are fitted by policy iteration. We play many games with the current f, record what each position actually cost, refit, and repeat. f must be part of the ${est.form} family (${est.description}), where x is log_2(n). The result is floored at 1, since one more guess is always needed.
